voice.text: Look at this giant canyon. The walls are taller than a hundred houses. [pause] Who carved it? A digger machine, [pause] or a river? Tap your guess.
When the seasons change, <emphasis>living things answer.</emphasis> Geese fly south. Trees drop their leaves. People pull on warm coats. [pause] Weather tells living things what to do next.

And the land? <emphasis>The land changes too.</emphasis> This river carved this whole canyon — little by little, a tiny bit of rock each year, for a very, very long time. [pause] Too slow to watch. But it never stopped.

At the beach, waves rub big rocks into pebbles, and pebbles into <emphasis>sand</emphasis> — that soft sand was hard rock once! [pause] And the wind piles the sand into dunes, and slowly walks them along the shore.
Some changes are <emphasis>fast</emphasis> — you can watch them happen! A storm snaps a branch in one crack. A flood picks up soil and drops it somewhere new in one afternoon.

Fast, or slow — wind and water are always at work. [pause] Even right now, too slow to see, the river is carving, the waves are grinding, the wind is pushing the dune. <emphasis>The land changes too.</emphasis>
Sort each change! Was it fast — quick enough to watch? Or slow — too slow to watch, but still happening? [pause] Drag the card, or tap a button.
All sorted! [pause] Now — detective time. Who did it, wind or water?
Be a land detective! Wind, or water — who made the change? Tap your answer.
Case closed, detective! [pause] Now show what you know.
Not quite. Could you stand and watch it happen? No — this takes years. [pause] It is still happening, just too slow to see.
Not quite. You could watch this one happen — that makes it fast.
Not quite. No machines, no shovels — nature's slow sculptor did this all by itself.
Not quite. It DID change — the land is always changing, just slowly.
Not quite. Seasons DO reach the animals — watch what they do when cold comes.
Not quite. Think: was it moving air, or moving water?
Not quite. Look again.
Yes! [pause] Years and years of carving — too slow to watch, but it never stopped.
Yes! [pause] One crack of the storm — you could watch it fall.
Yes! [pause] One wave, and whoosh — fast enough to watch.
Yes! [pause] Rain rusts the swing a tiny bit at a time, week after week.
Yes! [pause] The wind moves the dune a few grains at a time — too slow to watch.
Yes! [pause] One big flood can move soil in a single afternoon.
The canyon got deeper and deeper. Who did it?
The sand piled up into wavy dunes. Who did it?
The beach pebbles are smooth and round. Who did it?
Autumn comes — cold days ahead. What do the geese do?
Yes! [pause] The river is the sculptor — a little rock every year, for ages.
Yes! [pause] Wind piles the sand and slowly walks the dunes along.
Yes! [pause] Waves tumbled the rocks against each other until they went smooth.
Yes! [pause] Living things answer the seasons — geese fly, trees drop leaves, people bundle up.
Who made the deep canyon?
Do mountains and rocks ever change?
Which one is a FAST change?
Is a storm the only thing that changes the land?
Autumn turns cold. Why do the geese fly south?
<soft>You can read the land's story!</soft> [pause] Well done.
Good try! Let's watch the sculptors once more.
Lesson done! Now go outside with your parent and find one thing the weather has changed.
